evaluation_inputs.system_description: An Event framework where the application logic and framework are highly inter-dependent. The Main module is part of the framework, and the Event Manager interacts directly with application handlers. It features an Event Queue and a base Handler component extended by standard and application-specific handlers.

phase_1_discovery.initial_documentation_status: Fully developed architecture with class diagrams, component descriptions, and defined component interactions.
evaluator_inquiry_questions: Can the components of the architecture be reused for future projects?
Can the framework be expanded in the future to accommodate a new application or new components?
Will the system handle any input given by the user and handle invalid input?
Is the architecture consistent in behavior?
Can any new application-specific functionality be added to the architecture?
Can the system be modified in short time and cost-effective manner?
Does the architecture perform its event-processing task properly?

hardware_view_description: System accepts input via Command Line Interface (CLI)
Single processor execution implied (sequential event processing)
runtime_constraints: Events must be dispatched in a First-Come-First-Served (FIFO) pattern
System must maintain an 'idle wait' state until input is received
Application logic is embedded within framework components

quantitative_model_parameters.performance_proxy: Number of components involved in a transaction
quantitative_model_parameters.transaction_speed: Qualitative (Slow due to high number of components involved)

questions: Does the system allow unauthorized access?
Does the architecture portray data confidentiality?
Does the architecture process any task in the fastest possible speed?

raw_candidate_scenarios.description: No unauthorized access to the system
All operations are processed in fastest possible speed
Any failure should be followed by immediate recovery
User errors in using system should be handled
New demands on system functionality should be accommodated
Major parts of the framework should be re-usable for future architectures
Framework modification is cost-effective, fast and in minimal time
Components in framework interact in a coordinated manner
Framework expansion is possible to allow for more sophisticated options
Implementation allows for execution in different environments
Proper data encapsulation and secure data structures
Flexible implementation using other programming languages
Overall consistent behavior expected from the architecture
Framework should be complete, clear and perform exactly as required
Hook up multiple applications to the framework at same time
Change interface from command-driven to window-based

business_goals: Provide an Event framework to be used by an application
Handle and process events through component interaction
Allow application components to utilize the framework services
technical_constraints: Must handle system termination via STOP handler
Must maintain system in idle state until input is received

children.scenario_description: An unauthorized user attempts to access the system via the CLI; the system denies access to protected event-processing capabilities.
During event and handler processing, data passed among framework components remains encapsulated and protected.
When user input arrives at the CLI during normal sequential event processing on a single processor, the system processes the event as quickly as possible for the architecture’s constraints.
When a failure occurs during event processing or handler execution, the system recovers immediately and continues processing.
When the user provides invalid input at the CLI while the system is in idle-wait state, the system detects and handles the invalid input without breaking the flow.
Over repeated normal event-processing operations, the system maintains consistent behavior across runs and inputs within the supported scope.
When a new functional demand is introduced, the framework is extended without major redesign.
When a change request requires framework modification, the framework can be changed quickly and at low cost.
When the interface is changed from CLI to window-based, the framework is modified without major redesign of the internal event-processing logic.
When a future project needs the framework, major components can be reused with minimal adaptation.
When a new component or more sophisticated option must be added, the framework expands without major rework.
When more than one application is connected to the framework, multiple applications can share the framework without interference.
When framework components process an event through the defined interactions, the component interactions remain coordinated and consistent.
When the system is exercised according to its defined use cases, the framework performs the required event-processing task completely and clearly.

architectural_approaches.approach_name: Event-driven architecture with a single FIFO event queue
architectural_approaches.description: The architecture uses one Event Queue and dispatches events in first-come-first-served order under sequential execution with an idle-wait state until input is received.

addressed_attributes.rationale: The evidence shows a single FIFO path and sequential processing; this supports a simple event-processing flow, while the supplied model also states transaction speed is slow due to the number of components involved.
FIFO ordering and idle-wait behavior support predictable processing, although no explicit fault recovery mechanism is supplied.
A single queue and ordered dispatch support a consistent component interaction structure.

architectural_approaches.description: A single Event Manager directly interacts with application handlers and includes a STOP handler for termination behavior.

addressed_attributes.rationale: The evidence indicates the framework can dispatch events and terminate via the STOP handler.
Centralized dispatch helps keep interaction patterns consistent.
A deterministic control path is implied, but recovery behavior is not evidenced.

architectural_approaches.approach_name: Framework with embedded application logic and extensible handlers
architectural_approaches.description: A base Handler is extended by standard and application-specific handlers, while application logic is embedded within framework components and the framework is highly inter-dependent with the application.

addressed_attributes.rationale: The handler inheritance structure provides an extension path, but embedded application logic and high inter-dependence suggest change ripple effects.
The base handler abstraction supports some reuse, though tight coupling limits portability of the overall framework.
Direct framework-to-handler interaction supports the required event-processing flow.

architectural_approaches.description: The system accepts input via a CLI and is implied to execute on a single processor in a sequential event-processing model.

addressed_attributes.rationale: This supports the current operating model described in the supplied evidence.
UI changes may be invasive because the evidence suggests input handling and framework logic are tightly coupled.
